title: Playing in Cleveland with Little John and his Merry Men
summary: Little John bought him a pawnshop horn and took him to Cleveland's Globe Theater, his only long trip from Detroit.

bands.name: Little John and His Merry Men

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I knew Claude Black. He was one of the fellows hanging around, yeah.
Now from Detroit did you -- as a piano player -- did you venture out like to Toledo or wherever from Detroit? Did you do some run-outs?

At one time I went to Cleveland to play with a trumpeter whose name was John Wilson. He’s short in stature, so he called himself Little John, and he called his band the Merry Men. Little John and his Merry Men. We played a theater in Cleveland for about a week called the Globe Theater. There I met -- there was a singer and a comedian on the show. I had had -- I was not in possession of an instrument. I didn’t own an instrument, because all mine had been stolen. Little John liked my playing and wanted me to play with his band so badly he bought me an instrument from a pawn shop and took me to Cleveland. That’s the only time I really ventured out from the Detroit for any length of time. I’d gone to Toledo maybe once and to other suburbs of Detroit, you know, Mount Clemens, some of those other places, Pontiac.
